chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'When a man performs Hajj on behalf of his brother, or his father, or a man from the people, is it befitting for him to say something?' He said, 'Yes. He should say after entering into Ihram: O Allah, whatever befalls me during this journey of mine from fatigue, or hardship, or affliction, or untidiness, then recompense so-and-so for it, and recompense me for fulfilling it on his behalf.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi – similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication to recite when performing Hajj on behalf of someone else?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific supplication for Hajj al-Tamattu' or Qada, highlighting the Shia theological distinction where the performer retains the reward for the act of fulfillment while transferring the reward of hardships to the principal. This practice underscores the concept of spiritual vicarious performance, where the physical exertion of the pilgrim serves as a means of merit for the deceased or absent person, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man performs Hajj on behalf of his brother, or on behalf of his father, or on behalf of a man from the people. Is it befitting for him that he should be saying something?’

Heasws said: ‘Yes. He should be saying after having worn the Ihraam, ‘O Allahazwj! Whatever hits me during this journey of mine, from fatigue, or difficulties, or affliction, or untidiness, so Recompense so and so with regards to it, and Recompense me for fulfilling it on his behalf’.
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby – similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs al-Hajj for his brother or father or anyone else; what is proper for him to say? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, after assuming the state of Ihram he should say, ‘O Lord, for any fatigue, hardships, afflictions and shaken condition that I may have experienced on the way, grant reward to so and so and grant me reward for completing it on his behalf.’”
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan has narrated a similar Hadith.
